03 / ANNUAL REPORT

ANNUAL REPORT — DEFINITIONS

DEER REMAINING
Number of living deer on the property at the end of the year, after hunting, natural mortality, recruitment, and any overpopulation adjustment.
CARRYING CAPACITY
Maximum number of deer the property's available herbaceous forage and browse can support in the game, based on whichever forage resource is more limiting. It uses a fixed reference nutritional demand of one buck for every two does, so harvesting deer does not directly change capacity.
DOE SCORE
Estimated doe body-weight score in pounds for the upcoming season, calculated from the remaining deer population relative to carrying capacity: 120 lb at or below 50% of capacity, decreasing to 80 lb at 100% or above. Scores stay fixed during each hunting season.
AVG BUCK TARGET
Population-level reference antler score in inches, calculated as the doe score plus 20. This value serves as the game's genetic antler-potential center and trophy-harvest threshold; individual bucks vary around it.
MATURE BUCK AVERAGE
Average current antler score in inches of surviving bucks age 5 or older at the end of the year. Displays 0 when no mature bucks remain.
YEAR TROPHY AVERAGE
Average antler score in inches of bucks harvested as trophies during that hunting season. A trophy buck must score strictly above the season's buck target. Displays 0 if no trophy bucks were harvested. The final game score is the weighted average of all qualifying trophy bucks harvested across all 10 seasons, calculated after Year 10.

🏆 GAME COMPLETE

📷 PRE-SEASON CAMERA SURVEY RESULTS

Select any hunting block to review its pre-season camera photographs. Surveys detect approximately 80% of deer with a home range in that block. Results remain fixed throughout the hunting season.

🏆 GAME HISTORY & LEADERBOARD

Completed games are stored separately from the active game. Scores rank by the average antler score of trophy bucks harvested across all 10 seasons.

HOW TO PLAY: Improve habitat and balance deer numbers to grow larger bucks. Each deer has two permanent home-range blocks and uses one of them at random each day. Pre-season cameras detect 80% of eligible deer in each block; view the current season’s survey in its own section below the hunting season. Approach visible deer, harvest selectively or pass, and end the hunt at any time to advance the day. The score is the average antler score of trophy bucks harvested across all 10 seasons, finalized after Year 10. Game state saves automatically in this browser.

SIMULATION NOTES: Uses the numerical model in the supplied design document. Population health is density / carrying capacity. Carrying capacity uses a fixed 1:2 buck-to-doe reference demand (1,460 points per deer per forage resource), regardless of actual herd sex ratio. This version uses one global herd with a permanent two-block home range for each deer, and deterministic habitat production with randomized individual bucks. Food-plot outputs and burn stages are game values, not field estimates. Before Year 1 you can set initial years since burn. Between seasons, prescribed fire is a yes/no treatment that resets fire age to 1 year; otherwise fire age advances automatically; habitat capacity and next-season deer scores update before hunting resumes. The game uses 20 Bernoulli trials with a 6-inch step for genetic antler potential. All initial bucks are generated from the same starting doe-score-based genetic center. New games start at approximately 82.5% of carrying capacity, with a Year 1 doe score of 94 pounds and a buck genetic-potential center of 114 inches. Ties at the buck trophy threshold count as management bucks.
